pairs.subject: evidence-provenance-weighting
pairs.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevCompareSubmissions.tsx:26 rubricCompare returns `mixed` and a per-column `currency` (graded vs keyless template) so the cohort boundary can be labelled, but the compare surface takes only axes/columns/leaderByAxis and never renders either. A template-scored column's fit and axis scores sit in the same matrix as LLM-graded ones with nothing on screen marking the two instruments, which is the silent mixed-vintage comparison the re-baselining technique forbids.

techniques.evidence: app/features/tools/devcases/DevCompareSubmissions.tsx:26 The lib (app/_lib/devcase-compare.ts) computes `mixed`/`currency` and keeps template columns from leading an axis. This surface drops both fields (a grep for currency/mixed in the component finds only the authenticity band), so the rendered table never says the cohort spans two scoring regimes.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevEvalPanel.tsx:132 The display is honest downward: 'observed' renders only when the bundle explicitly carries tooling=observed. Any missing or other value renders 'inferred' in muted styling, so an unestablished basis never borrows the observed badge.

app/features/tools/devcases/DevHelpers.ts:44 The default sits at the lookup's definition (describeSource, same directory, used by DevProvenanceStrip). An absent or unrecognised source resolves to the weakest descriptor (template/deterministic, muted), not to 'llm'. This governs step-source display, not skill-claim scoring.
